title: Teaching RILL the editor services
why: Keep the established compiler and add only the service names needed by a screen editor. Share the built-in lookup instead of copying its scanner.

title: Binding the new intermediate operations
why: Define screen positions, key events and bounded transfers in the intermediate language. Keep BIOS calls, native registers and segments inside an explicit target binding.

title: Taking charge of the text screen
why: Enter and leave an existing 80-column text mode, preserving its cursor settings. A failed entry must return to DOS without leaving an active screen session.

title: Writing a counted screen row
why: Write a counted span of cells with a stable attribute. Position zero is the upper left; the last status row must not scroll the document.

title: Reading navigation keys
why: Translate the keyboard into character values and named event numbers. The editor needs arrows and function keys without knowing BIOS scan codes.

title: Transferring bytes between storage blocks
why: Copy counted bytes between a near I/O buffer and an allocated block. Validate the complete source and destination extents before changing memory.

title: Moving overlapping text safely
why: Move bytes within or between allocated blocks, including overlap. A gap buffer must preserve text when either copy direction overlaps its source.

title: Counting past a word boundary
why: Represent document positions as low and high words. A 256 KiB document needs carry, borrow and complete-position comparisons.

title: Allocating the document pages
why: Obtain eight separately allocated 32 KiB pages. Release every successful allocation even if a later request fails.

title: Reading a file into the pages
why: Read EDIT.TXT through a 4096-byte buffer into the pages. Count every positive read, distinguish an absent file from an I/O failure, and reject excess input.

title: Saving through a temporary file
why: Write the occupied document ranges into EDIT.TMP and publish a closed file. Preserve the accepted EDIT.TXT and retain recovery files when restoration fails.

title: Keeping free space at the cursor
why: Move the gap to a requested logical position without changing the document. Clip each transfer at both page boundaries and copy in the safe direction.

title: Finding physical line boundaries
why: Locate beginnings and endings without building a full line index. Treat CR/LF as a pair while also accepting bare CR and LF.

title: Measuring columns and tab stops
why: Count visual columns separately from byte positions. Expand tabs to stops eight columns apart and retain the desired column across unequal line lengths.

title: Painting a window on the document
why: Draw twenty-four document rows and one status row. Keep a horizontal window for long lines and show control bytes without changing the stored file.

title: Moving the insertion position
why: Connect navigation keys to the gap and window. Preserve the preferred column for vertical movement and keep the cursor visible after a scroll.

title: Inserting text and line endings
why: Insert printable characters, tabs and CR/LF at the gap. Track unsaved changes and ask before discarding them.

title: Deleting text at either side
why: Delete one character or one complete line ending. Repaint the affected line, or the window when the line layout changes.

title: Remembering edits for undo
why: Keep a bounded ring of edit records in one extra block. Reverse insertion or deletion without copying the complete document.

title: Finding a literal string
why: Find literal text from the current position and repeat the search from the next byte. Search the document through logical positions, including page boundaries.
